title: Empirical restricted Fourier weight concentration
statement: Let $f$ be a sign-valued function on the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube, let $J\subseteq[n]$, and let $S\subseteq J$. For each triple of cube inputs, split each input into its coordinates in $J$ and outside $J$, use the outside coordinates of the first input as a fixed assignment, and use the $J$-coordinates of the second and third inputs as two free assignments; let the observation be the product of the two values of $f$ at the resulting cube points, each multiplied by the monomial on $S$ of its free assignment. If $m>0$ independent uniform triples are sampled and their observations are averaged, then for every $\varepsilon\ge 0$, the probability that this average differs from the sum of squared Fourier coefficients of $f$ over frequencies formed by adjoining any outside-$J$ frequency to $S$ by at least $\varepsilon$ is at most $2\exp(-m\varepsilon^2/2)$.
hypotheses_covered: A sign-valued function on the $n$-dimensional cube
